original_question: A planar billiard table Y is called integrable when the set of invariant circles of its billiard map has nonempty interior. Must every such integrable billiard table be an ellipse?
target_in_paper: Problem 1 (Birkhoff conjecture) in §2: "Ellipses are the only integrable billiard tables." The relevant notion of integrability is the one given immediately before it in Definition 1. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it uses the billiard-map notion of integrability from Definition 1 and asks whether every such integrable planar billiard must be an ellipse, which is exactly the content of Problem 1. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: The paper's statement appears in §2 under the heading "Smooth, strictly convex billiard: elliptic dynamics," so a fully stand-alone version should say that Y is a smooth strictly convex planar billiard table, not just an arbitrary planar table. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

An "invariant circle" here is not an arbitrary invariant closed curve: it is a φ-invariant noncontractible topological circle in the annular phase space of the billiard map. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The "nonempty interior" is interior in the billiard map's phase space, not in the physical domain Y. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To make the question self-contained, the billiard map should be identified as the Poincaré return map on the annular phase space attached to the boundary of Y. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper explicitly treats the disc as a degenerate ellipse, so the conclusion should allow that special case. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The paper separately formulates a Hamiltonian-flow variant as Problem 1a and says that solving Problem 1 and Problem 1a would not directly imply one another, so the refined question should stay with billiard-map integrability and not switch to Hamiltonian integrability. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

There are no ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or "for all sufficiently large m" conditions in this problem; the missing information is geometric and dynamical rather than algebraic. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let Y be a bounded connected planar billiard table with smooth strictly convex boundary, and let φ:Φ(Y)→Φ(Y) be its billiard map on the annular phase space Φ(Y). Call Y integrable if the set of φ-invariant noncontractible topological circles in Φ(Y) has nonempty interior in Φ(Y). Must Y be an ellipse (allowing the disc as a degenerate ellipse)? ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The draft is aiming at the survey's official Problem 1, not at a broader neighboring problem. In §2 the paper first defines integrability via invariant circles of the billiard map (Definition 1) and then states verbatim: "Ellipses are the only integrable billiard tables." In §5.1 the author introduces Problem 1a for Hamiltonian integrability of the billiard flow and immediately notes that resolving either Problem 1 or Problem 1a would not directly imply the other, so broadening the draft to that variant would move away from the paper's exact intent. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/ErgodicUnder2024/ApplicationsBilliardsII.pdf?utm_source=openai))

citations.label: Definition of invariant circle in the paragraph preceding Definition 1
Problem 1a and the remark that Problems 1 and 1a do not directly imply one another
